import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(18, 12))
fig.suptitle('Coffee Shop Sales Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# 1. Sales by Product
product_sales = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
axes[0, 0].bar(product_sales.index, product_sales.values, color='#8B4513')
axes[0, 0].set_title('Total Sales by Product')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Product')
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Sales by Age Group
age_sales = df.groupby('customer_age_group')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
axes[0, 1].barh(age_sales.index, age_sales.values, color='#D2691E')
axes[0, 1].set_title('Total Sales by Age Group')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Total Sales ($)')
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Age Group')

# 3. Payment Method Distribution
payment_counts = df.groupby('payment_method').size()
colors = ['#CD853F', '#DEB887']
axes[0, 2].pie(payment_counts.values, labels=payment_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
               colors=colors, startangle=90)
axes[0, 2].set_title('Payment Method Distribution')

# 4. Takeaway vs Dine-in
takeaway_sales = df.groupby('is_takeaway')['total'].sum()
labels = ['Dine-in', 'Takeaway']
axes[1, 0].bar(labels, takeaway_sales.values, color=['#A0522D', '#F4A460'])
axes[1, 0].set_title('Sales by Service Type')
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)')

# 5. Sales by Size
size_order = ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large']
size_sales = df.groupby('size')['total'].sum()
size_sales = size_sales.reindex(size_order, fill_value=0)
axes[1, 1].bar(size_sales.index, size_sales.values, color='#BC8F8F')
axes[1, 1].set_title('Total Sales by Size')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Size')
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)')

# 6. Quantity Distribution
quantity_counts = df.groupby('quantity').size()
axes[1, 2].bar(quantity_counts.index, quantity_counts.values, color='#DAA520')
axes[1, 2].set_title('Order Quantity Distribution')

axes[1, 2].set_ylabel('Number of Orders')
